plurals.item: Add as many languages as you want. Swipe on the spacebar to change language, or press the 🌐 key. All %1$d language is built in, so add the one you need now or later in Settings, then Languages.
Add as many languages as you want. Swipe on the spacebar to change language, or press the 🌐 key. All %1$d languages are built in, so add the ones you need now or later in Settings, then Languages.

resources.string: These come from the language settings and the region of your device. The app does not read what you type, and no data leaves your device.

The keyboard downloads the word list and the prediction data for each language you add here. The download runs in the background over your current connection. You can delete the data later in Settings, then Languages.
Every language is already in your list.
This language has more than one layout or input system, and most people use only one of them. Select the ones you want. You can change them later in Settings, then Languages.

resources.string: Select how the keyboard looks. AMOLED is fully black for OLED screens.
Select one theme for each. The keyboard changes with your device.
Some people want a signal for each key press. Other people want silence. The strength, the duration and the popups are in Typing settings.
The device vibrates on each key press
The device makes a click sound on each key press
A bubble shows the character above the key you press
A sideways swipe on the spacebar is the fastest way to change language or move the text cursor. Select what it does.
A quick swipe moves the cursor. Press and hold, then swipe to change language
A quick swipe changes the language. Press and hold, then swipe to move the cursor
Each swipe on the spacebar goes to your next language
Each swipe on the spacebar moves the text cursor
The keyboard ignores swipes on the spacebar
The 🌐 key becomes an emoji key. This is useful when the spacebar changes the language
A row of the numbers 1 to 0 above the letters
The toolbox holds everything from GIFs to a calculator behind the grid button on the toolbar. Start with only the tools you use. You can turn each one on or off at any time in Tools settings.
Some of the tools you turned on have their own choices. You can change all of them later in the settings of each tool.
The tool always shows the Gregorian date. The calendars below show next to it
The month grid shows it next to the Gregorian month, and in each day cell
One more calendar for the header and the day you select
Turn this off to see the temperature in Celsius
The compass rose marks the direction of the Kaaba
The qibla direction uses the same saved place as the weather tool.
Three quick questions. All of them optional.
How many languages do you type in?
Both spacebar swipes now change the language. You can give one back to the cursor on the next pages.
What kind of keyboard do you want?
A small set of tools, fewer setup pages, and the simple settings.
The tools most people use, and the standard settings.
All pages, every tool to pick from, and every setting.
A few things this keyboard does that most keyboards cannot. Flip on what sounds useful.
Type 12*8= or 20 usd in eur and the answer appears above the keys, ready to insert.
Type a tool’s name, like translate, and a chip appears that opens it.
Over 70 tools behind one key: translate, scan text, calculator, GIFs, QR codes, a password generator and more.
Pick your tools in Settings, then Tools.
Put your own photo, or one searched online, behind the keys. Rotate them on a schedule.
Find them in Appearance, then Themes.
A full copy history, plus chips that pull codes, phone numbers and links out of what you copy.
Short triggers that expand into full text, with fill-in patterns.
Set them up in the snippets tool.
One-time codes appear as a chip above the keys the moment they arrive.
Needs notification access. The keyboard asks for it on first use.
Write in script, bubble, bold and more styles that work in any app.
Rewrite, translate or chat with an AI, right from the keyboard.
Bring your own API key. Finish setup later in Tools, then AI.
Voice typing that runs fully on the phone. No internet needed.
Download a model in the voice tool’s settings.
A different keyboard for each app: its own layout, theme and tools.
Build them in Settings, then Modes.
Everything you chose is live. Type a little and see how it feels.
Type 12*8= and watch the answer appear above the keys
Type translate and tap the chip that appears
